title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
provenance: Reported by Michael-Liendo (highball-db#283, 2026-10-02), Apple M4, macOS 27.0, Highball 0.10.2, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r17, Wine's Direct3D, rated 5 of 5 after 8 minutes once set up, recipe steam. Not verified by the maintainer. bindigga (highball-db#1300, 2026-11-18), Apple M3, macOS 26.4, Highball 0.10.26, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28, DXMT, rated 3 of 5 after 6 minutes: named gta-sa in the report (gta_sa in the title) with no Steam id, taken to be the Steam release (12120). It failed to start with 'Cannot find 800x600x32 video mode' until the player installed a few community fixes they don't name, then ran the intro cutscene and about 5 minutes of riding the bike at a smooth 60 fps with very minor stutter.
notes: The 2005 original, which Steam no longer sells (its store page says it is no longer available; Rockstar sells the Definitive Edition instead), so this row is for people who already own it. Reported playable on Wine's own Direct3D on the default engine after two changes: the game refuses to start without Wine's virtual desktop, and DXVK was very slow in the menus and in play where Wine's Direct3D ran well. Inside the virtual desktop window there is no real fullscreen. A DualSense controller worked after the two WineBus registry values that Highball's Controllers through SDL tweak sets. Nothing was measured here. A later report on an M3 with the default engine r28, in DXMT mode, got past the 800x600x32 error with community fixes the player doesn't name, then played smoothly at 60 fps (highball-db#1300).

knownIssues.symptom: Fails to start with 'Cannot find 800x600x32 video mode' (reported on an M4, macOS 27.0, engine r17)
knownIssues.cause: Not investigated here. The game asks for an 800x600 32-bit display mode at startup and gets none it accepts without a virtual desktop
knownIssues.fix: Turn on Wine's virtual desktop for the game: under HKCU\Software\Wine\Explorer set Desktop to Default, with a Desktops\Default size matching the in-game resolution. The reporter did this by hand in the registry. There is no native fullscreen inside that window. A player on an M3 got past it with a few community fixes instead, without naming them (highball-db#1300)

knownIssues.symptom: Very slow on DXVK, in the menus and in play (reported on an M4)
knownIssues.fix: Set the game's graphics mode to Wine's Direct3D (wined3d), which the reporter says runs well

knownIssues.symptom: A DualSense controller is not seen by the game (reported on an M4)
knownIssues.cause: Wine's controller driver reads the pad through the Mac's raw HID path as well as SDL, and some games only see it through SDL
knownIssues.fix: Apply the Controllers through SDL tweak from the environment's recipes (it sets Enable SDL and DisableHidraw under HKCU\Software\Wine\WineBus, the two values the reporter set by hand), then restart the environment
